mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm glad you're here. Together, we're about to dive into a story that's as dramatic as it is thought-provoking. Imagine a revolution that once promised liberation, equality, and a new world—only to find itself tangled in contradiction and struggle. That’s the journey Leon Trotsky takes us on in The Revolution Betrayed, where he explores the fate of the Soviet experiment from the inside out. We’ll look at those powerful ideals of 1917—workers in charge, real social justice, the end of oppression—and see how they faced off against the harsh reality that emerged under Stalin. What happens when hope collides with power? How does progress get derailed, even when the dream is so bold? Trotsky’s own life, first as a revolutionary leader and then as an exile, gives this story a personal edge—a sense that these questions aren’t just historical, but deeply human. As we go further, you and I will explore how the Soviet Union changed, looking through the lens of its economy, its shifting classes, and the people who rose to power. The rise of bureaucracy, the silencing of voices, and the loss of democracy aren’t just events of the past—they’re cautionary tales for anyone who cares about change. The Revolution Betrayed doesn’t just recount history; it asks us to reflect on the paradoxes of progress, the price of compromise, and the ongoing struggle to turn ideals into reality. So, as we set off on this exploration, let’s keep our minds open, our curiosity sharp, and see what lessons we can uncover—together—about the forces that shape societies when everything is up for grabs.
